title: Construction Project Manager Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide
description: Convert a construction project manager salary from hourly to annual. Includes 38-hour week, fortnightly pay, tax, super, and casual loading. Based on Fair Work and ABS data.
salarySummary: For a construction project manager earning the industry average of $1985.30 per week (38 hours), the annual salary is approximately $103,235.60 before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the construction project manager salary include super?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your base salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer must add $12,000 to your super fund.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the construction industry average and a job median for a project manager?
faqs.a: The construction industry average of $1985.30 per week (from ABS May 2026) is an average for all full-time construction workers, not a median for a specific role. A construction project manager salary may be higher or lower depending on experience, location, and award coverage.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Construction Project Manager Salary

If you are a construction project manager or considering a role in this field, you likely want to know how an hourly rate translates into an annual salary, fortnightly pay, and what you can expect after tax and super. This guide uses Australian data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, Australian Bureau of Statistics, and Australian Taxation Office to give you a clear picture. We focus on the **construction project manager salary** as an industry average, not a job-specific median, because the ABS provides a broad average for construction full-time ordinary time workers.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard conversion is: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. Most full-time roles in Australia assume a 38-hour week, as per the National Employment Standards. So if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross salary is $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly. This formula is used on [the timesheet](/) where you can type your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### Fortnightly Pay

Fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay multiplied by two. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. For a $50 per hour rate at 38 hours, weekly pay is $1,900, and fortnightly pay is $3,800. This is useful for budgeting and comparing to salary offers that quote a fortnightly figure.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, many construction project managers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for specific awards. Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum rate.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual construction project manager, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. On [the timesheet](/) there is a checkbox to add this loading automatically. Importantly, you should never type a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator adds it for you. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (super guarantee) from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer contributes an extra $12,000 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a construction project manager earning $100,000 per year, the tax (excluding Medicare) would be approximately $22,967, plus $2,000 Medicare, leaving about $75,033 take-home pay. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed estimate.

### The Construction Industry Average

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings in construction at $1,985.30 per week. This is an **industry average**, not a median for a construction project manager. The average for all employees (including part-time) is $1,579.20 per week. The full-time average for all industries is $2,083.70 per week. So a construction project manager salary could be above or below this average depending on your role, experience, and location. For more data, see [reference tables](/data).

### Example: Construction Project Manager Salary Calculation

Let's say you are a construction project manager earning the industry average of $1,985.30 per week. Assuming a 38-hour week, your hourly rate is $1,985.30 ÷ 38 = $52.24 per hour. Your annual gross salary is $1,985.30 × 52 = $103,235.60. Fortnightly pay is $1,985.30 × 2 = $3,970.60. After tax (using the 2026–27 rates) and Medicare, your annual take-home pay would be approximately $76,500. Super at 12% adds $12,388.27 to your super fund, paid on top.

If you are a casual construction project manager, add 25% loading to the hourly rate: $52.24 × 1.25 = $65.30 per hour. Then annual gross becomes $65.30 × 38 × 52 = $129,032.80. Super is still 12% of ordinary earnings (the base rate, not including loading) – but check your award as some awards treat loading as ordinary earnings for super. The Fair Work Ombudsman clarifies that casual loading is part of ordinary earnings for super. For more on this, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Important Distinctions

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 casual. This is the legal minimum for non-award employees. A construction project manager salary is typically much higher.
- **Award rates**: Specific awards like the Building and Construction Award may set higher minimums for project managers. Always check your award coverage.
- **Casual loading**: 25% loading on base rate, super on top.
- **Super**: Super guarantee 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, not deducted from pay.

### Limitations of This Estimate

Annual pay here is hourly × hours per week × 52. It assumes same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice. Super estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, stops at $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax 2026-27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare 2025-26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, salary packaging not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For a personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/) and consult a professional.
